rules.description: EEO-1 Component 1 annual workforce demographic report

value.federalContractorCriteria: federal contractors with 50 or more employees meeting certain criteria (EEOC)

versions.notes: Long-standing rule; in force before this date. Earlier history is not modelled — effectiveFrom is the modelling baseline, not the date the rule was enacted. STATUS (Oct 2026): 2024 collection closed; EEOC says updates on the 2025 collection will be posted. On 21 Jul 2026 the EEOC voted to issue an NPRM to rescind EEO-1 to EEO-6 reporting (see https://www.eeoc.gov/newsroom/eeoc-proposes-rescission-annual-race-and-sex-reporting-requirements). The requirement remains in the regulations until a final rule; review when the rule is finalised. Federal contractor criteria (e.g. contract value) not modelled. Phase 5 (verified 2026-10-18): job categories (Officials and Managers split into Executive/Senior Level and First/Mid Level, ten in all), race/ethnicity categories (Hispanic or Latino, then not Hispanic or Latino: White, Black or African American, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, Asian, American Indian or Alaska Native, Two or More Races), male/female columns, self-identification preferred and employment records or observer identification if the employee declines: EEO-1 Instruction Booklet on eeoc.gov (https://www.eeoc.gov/sites/default/files/migrated_files/employers/eeo1/instruction_rev_2006.pdf). Its July-September payroll period is superseded: the workforce snapshot is one pay period from 1 October to 31 December of the reporting year (EEOC Commission meeting transcript, 11 August 2026, https://www.eeoc.gov/meetings/notice-commission-hearing-August-11/transcript). The current booklet is on eeocdata.org (not allow-listed): legal review.

rules.description: FLSA white-collar, computer, outside sales and highly compensated exemptions: duties criteria and which salary test applies (29 CFR part 541)

source.title: U.S. DOL WHD Fact Sheet #17A — Exemption for Executive, Administrative, Professional, Computer & Outside Sales Employees

versions.notes: Fact Sheet #17A (revised September 2019) summarises 29 CFR part 541: executive, administrative, learned and creative professional, computer (salary level or at least $27.63 an hour), outside sales (no salary test) and highly compensated (total annual compensation from overtime.exempt_salary_threshold, at least one exempt duty). Up to 10% of the standard salary level may be met by nondiscretionary bonuses paid at least annually. effectiveFrom aligns with the restored 2019 salary levels (overtime.exempt_salary_threshold); earlier periods are not modelled. Teachers and practitioners of law or medicine (no salary test, 29 CFR 541.303-304) are not modelled; ecfr.gov blocked automated fetching.

rules.description: Form I-9 completion deadlines: Section 1 by the first day of employment, Section 2 within three business days

source.title: USCIS M-274 Handbook for Employers — 4.0 Completing Section 2

versions.notes: M-274 4.0: "Within three business days of the date employment begins, you or your authorized representative must complete Section 2"; example: employment begins Monday -> Section 2 on or before Thursday; hire for less than three business days -> Section 2 no later than the first day of employment. Section 1: employee completes no later than the first day of employment, not before accepting the job offer (Form I-9 instructions, edition 01/20/25, https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/forms/i-9instr.pdf). USCIS does not define "business days": the tenant configures its business weekdays (default Monday to Friday). Long-standing rule; effectiveFrom is the modelling baseline shared with the other i9.* keys.
